title: SCIM provisioning: checkpointed reconcile, manual restore, and operator rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers have reported hard-to-reproduce user loss and partial group membership drift after transient failures during SCIM bulk deprovision runs. Current retry strategies cause duplicated operations or missed items when jobs are interrupted, and operators lack a safe manual restore workflow. Goal: implement a checkpointed reconcile engine with durable per-tenant cursors, idempotent operation semantics, a dead-letter store for unrecoverable items, and an operator-facing restore/rollback playbook integrated with audit logs and RBAC v2 controls.
acceptance_criteria: Reconcile job persists progress cursor per-tenant and can resume from last checkpoint after crash or restart without duplicating side-effects
Deprovision operations are idempotent or guarded by tombstone markers so repeated retries do not create inconsistent state
Items that fail beyond retry/backoff thresholds land in a discoverable dead-letter store with an explict restore action
Operator UI exposes tenant-level reconcile status, failed item list, and a one-click manual restore that records audit events and requires admin permission
End-to-end tests validate resume behavior, concurrent reconcile safety, and audit log entries for all admin restore/rollback actions
No customer user is permanently deleted without a documented deprovision timestamp and an operator confirmation window (configurable TTL)
Performance regression <5% on regular provisioning throughput after enabling checkpointing
implementation_notes: Add a durable checkpoint table in primary metadata DB keyed by tenant+job-type with last_processed_id, last_updated_at, and attempt_count
Make SCIM mutations idempotent by recording operation_id and using upsert semantics for user/group state; when not feasible use tombstone flags and a recoverable delete window
Use exponential backoff with jitter per-item and escalate to dead-letter after N attempts (configurable per-tenant)
Dead-letter store schema must include original payload, failure reason, last_attempt_ts, and reconciliation cursor snapshot to allow targeted reprocessing

Expose operator actions via Console with RBAC v2 gating: only users in admin role can execute restore/freeze/unfreeze actions and these actions emit audit-log entries with requestor, reason, and before/after snapshots
Integrate with existing audit logging pipeline for SSO events so restores link back to the originating SCIM provider event and SAML assertion ID where available
Design reconciliation to batch by streamable key ranges to limit memory usage and allow parallel workers per-tenant
Add metrics: reconcile_progress_seconds, items_retried_total, dead_letter_count, manual_restores_total, restore_latency_seconds
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged rollout for 2 internal tenants — enable checkpointing and dead-letter capture only (no auto-restore) — 1 week
Phase 2: Expand to 20 early-adopter customers with console read-only visibility into dead-letter contents — 2 weeks
Phase 3: Enable operator restore UI behind RBAC for internal support team; collect audit logs and run simulated restores — 1 week
Phase 4: Gradual customer opt-in with automated retries configured, monitor metrics and error bursts for 2 weeks
Phase 5: Global enablement and remove long tail feature flags after 30 days stable metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint CRUD, idempotent operation guards, tombstone lifecycle
Integration tests that simulate process restarts during middle of bulk deprovision and assert resume semantics
Chaos test: randomly kill reconcile worker at varying intervals and assert no user loss or duplicate state changes
E2E staging run with mirrored customer data and manual restore exercised by SRE
Security test: attempt restores via non-admin accounts and assert RBAC denies and logs the attempt
